t.d: Rigid school backpack derived from the Dutch military ransel, standard for Japanese elementary pupils since Gakushūin adopted it.
t.tech: stitched firm leather over a stiff box body
t.auth: workshop or department-store make, genuine leather or cordovan versus Clarino; price bands from about ¥30,000 to over ¥100,000

t.d: French trunk-making houses that built flat, canvas-covered travelling trunks for rail and steamship travel.
t.tech: wooden frame covered in canvas or leather, with slats, metal corners, rivets and locks
t.mat: poplar, beech, coated canvas, leather, brass
t.auth: original labels, serial numbers and canvas type date a trunk

t.p: Tang dynasty onward; common by the Ming
t.d: Bamboo-framed paper umbrellas waterproofed with tung oil and painted.
t.tech: bamboo frame tied with string; paper glued, trimmed, oiled and sun-dried; painted
t.mat: bamboo, paper, tung oil, persimmon juice
t.auth: hand-tied bamboo frame, oiled paper canopy, hand painting

t.p: late 19th century onward; in Pathein from 1914
t.d: Hand-made Burmese umbrellas descended from royal craftsmen of King Thibaw's court.
t.tech: entirely by hand: frame, canopy binding, Tasae dyeing, oiling, painting, polishing
t.mat: Taragu bamboo, Ma U Shwe War wood, oiled cotton or silk
t.auth: aged Taragu bamboo ribs, hand-painted oiled cotton

t.p: Muromachi period onward; peak in the Shōwa period
t.d: Japanese bamboo-and-washi umbrellas developed from the Chinese oil-paper umbrella.
t.tech: over a hundred hand procedures in Gifu; oiled and painted paper
t.auth: hand-made bamboo ribs and washi canopy

t.p: Meiji period to present; traditional craft 2003
t.d: Chiba flat fans with a round bamboo handle and a lattice 'window' of thread-bound ribs.
t.tech: one medake culm split into about 48–64 ribs, interlaced with thread, curved support of madake
t.mat: medake and madake bamboo; washi, silk or cotton
t.auth: round handle and semicircular lattice window

t.d: Hangzhou folding-fan craft, best known for persimmon-lacquered black paper fans.
t.tech: some 86 steps: bamboo shaving, lime boiling, heat straightening, pasting, hand-pleating, persimmon-tannin colouring
t.mat: wild brown bamboo, Tianmu mulberry paper, Zhuji persimmon lacquer, buffalo-horn rivets

t.p: Nanboku-chō roots; Edo-period Gosho uchiwa; traditional craft 1977
t.d: Kyoto flat fans whose ribs and handle are made separately, historically painted by court painters.
t.tech: sashie construction: ribs inserted into a separate handle
t.auth: separate handle (sashie); fine pieces have 50–100 ribs

t.p: early Heian period to present; traditional craft 1977
t.d: Kyoto folding fans of bamboo ribs and paper or silk, made by many specialist artisans.
t.tech: rib splitting and polishing, leaf pasting, gold leaf, hand painting or woodblock printing, folding (some 87 processes)
t.mat: madake, hachiku or moso bamboo; washi, silk; cypress, cedar or sandalwood for wooden fans; gold, silver or tin foil

t.p: early Edo period to present; traditional craft 1997
t.d: Flat bamboo fans first sold to Kotohira Shrine pilgrims; Marugame now makes most of Japan's uchiwa.
t.tech: handle and ribs split from one piece of bamboo; flat-handle style dominant since Meiji
t.auth: one-piece bamboo frame; most output is machine-made plastic, bamboo fans are hand-made

t.r: Valencia and l'Horta, incl. Aldaia, Spain
t.d: Spain's main fan centre, making painted paper and silk folding fans, about 70% of Spanish output.
t.tech: leaf cut and pleated, painted in gouache, mounted on the monture and riveted
t.mat: laid paper or silk leaves; wood or bone sticks

t.r: Papua New Guinea; also western New Guinea and the Solomon Islands
t.d: Looped string bags, mostly made by women and sold in markets; the name also covers the technique.
t.tech: knotless looping, fibre spun as it is looped
t.mat: plant fibre, fur, wool, cotton, commercial yarn
t.auth: looped, not knitted or crocheted; the fabric does not unravel round a break

t.d: Handwoven bags of vegetable twine with leather trim, indigenous to the Taita, Kikuyu and Kamba peoples.
Crocheted bags made by Wayuu women, who learn the craft young; men make the straps.
t.mat: acrylic thread today; plant-dyed cotton traditionally
t.auth: made by Wayuu weavers; acrylic thread is standard today, not cotton
